title: Fix root Makefile's audit/analyze/test-all targets so they stop reporting false passes

evidence.quote:
cd learning_tracker && dart run custom_lint; \
	echo "audit PASSED."

why: The whole `audit` recipe is one shell invocation (backslash-continued); its final two statements are joined by `;`, not `&&`, so the recipe's exit status is that of the LAST command (`echo "audit PASSED."`), never custom_lint's. Empirically reproduced: a `false;`-then-`echo` recipe in a throwaway Makefile prints the trailing text and `make` still exits 0. Since custom_lint is currently broken (crashes, per baseline), running `make audit` from the repo root today prints the crash output and then unconditionally declares "audit PASSED." Separately, root `analyze` omits `--fatal-infos` and `test-all` omits `--coverage`, unlike learning_tracker/Makefile's equivalents (which say "matches CI --fatal-infos flag" and are correct) — so `make ci` from repo root can go green on issues the real CI gate (which always runs from learning_tracker/) would reject.
recommendation: Replace the trailing `;` with `&&` (or check `$?` explicitly) so a lint failure fails the recipe; add `--fatal-infos` to root `analyze` and `--coverage` to root `test-all`, or better, make the root Makefile's targets thin `cd learning_tracker && make $@` wrappers so there is exactly one place these flags can drift.
acceptance_criteria: `make audit` from the repo root exits non-zero when the underlying custom_lint invocation fails.
root `make analyze` uses --fatal-infos and root `make test-all`/`ci` produce coverage output, matching learning_tracker/Makefile.
